verses.text: Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name. Let every people know what he’s done.
Sing to him! Sing his praises and tell about every wonder he’s worked.
Take pride in his holy name. Let the hearts of everyone looking for the LORD fill with joy.
Look to the LORD and his strength. Keep seeking his face.
Remember the amazing things he’s done, the wonders he worked and the judgments he spoke,
you descendants of his servant Abraham, you children of Jacob whom he chose.
He’s the LORD our God. His judgments reach across the whole earth.
He remembers his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations.
It’s the covenant he made with Abraham and the oath he swore to Isaac.
He confirmed it to Jacob as a law, to Israel as a covenant that lasts forever.
He said, “I’ll give you the land of Canaan. That’s the share you’ll inherit.”
He said it when they were only a handful of people, strangers in the land.
They moved from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He let no one mistreat them. He even called out kings for their sake:
“Keep your hands off my anointed ones! Don’t do a thing to harm my prophets!”
He called down famine on the land and cut off their food supply.
He sent someone ahead of them. Joseph was sold as a slave.
Shackles bruised his feet, and an iron collar locked around his neck,
until what he’d said came true and the LORD’s word proved him right.
The king, a ruler over peoples, sent for him and set him free.
He put Joseph in charge of his household and everything he owned,
with authority to discipline his officials as he saw fit and teach his elders wisdom.
Then Israel came to Egypt, and Jacob made his home in the land of Ham.
God made his people grow in number until they were stronger than their enemies.
He turned the Egyptians’ hearts against his people, and they plotted against his servants.
He sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron, the man he had chosen.
They worked miracles in front of the people and did wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and the land went dark. They didn’t rebel against his words.
He turned their water to blood and killed their fish.
Frogs swarmed over the land and got into the rooms of their kings.
He spoke, and swarms of flies came, with lice all across their land.
He sent hail instead of rain, and lightning flashed through their land.
He struck their vines and fig trees and shattered the trees across the country.
He spoke, and locusts and grasshoppers came in numbers no one could count.
They ate every plant in the land and devoured everything the ground produced.
He struck down all the firstborn in the land, the first fruits of their strength.
He led his people out with silver and gold, and no one among his tribes was too weak to keep up.
Egypt was glad to see them leave, because the people were terrified of them.
He spread a cloud over them for shelter and gave them fire to light up the night.
They asked for food, so he brought them quail and filled them with bread from the sky.
He opened the rock, and water gushed out. It ran like a river through the dry ground.
He remembered his holy promise and his servant Abraham.
He brought his people out rejoicing. The ones he chose came out singing.
He gave them the lands of the nations, and they took possession of what those peoples had worked for,
so they could keep his statutes and follow his laws. Praise the LORD!
